name: Quad set
summary: Tighten the thigh and press the back of the knee down. The first exercise after most knee surgery.
setup: Sit or lie with the leg straight, side-on to the phone at floor level. A rolled towel under the knee is fine. Tighten the front of the thigh so the kneecap draws up, hold, relax.
why: Almost nothing moves — the kneecap glides a centimetre. A camera cannot judge the squeeze, so this one is logged by hand.
progression: Straight leg raise once the thigh can lock the knee.
regression: Shorter squeezes, or with the knee slightly bent over a towel.
contraindications: Sharp pain in the joint, or a knee that will not straighten without swelling increasing.

faults.label: Knee bending instead of pressing down
faults.cue: Press the back of the knee down
faults.tip: The back of the knee should flatten toward the floor. If the heel lifts, the hip is doing the work.

faults.label: Letting go too soon
faults.tip: The squeeze has to last for the muscle to learn it. Count it out loud.

faults.label: Holding the breath
faults.tip: Count out loud through the squeeze so the breath cannot stop.

faults.label: Pointing the toes
faults.tip: Pulling the toes up helps the thigh switch on; pointing them lets the calf take over.

guide.surface: Firm floor or mat, or a bed if getting down is hard.
guide.stop: Sharp pain inside the joint, or swelling that grows during the session.
guide.cannotSee: The squeeze itself — the phone sees a still leg. It confirms position only.

points.t: Leg straight, toes pointing up, heel resting on the floor.
Kneecap draws up toward the hip as the thigh tightens.
Sit tall or lie flat; no bracing with the arms.
